cards.title: Optimize WordPress permalinks and strip default plugins after install
cards.summary: Configure clean post-name URLs and deactivate bundled plugins before building a WooCommerce store, so product URLs stay readable and the site isn't bloated.
cards.use_when: You've just installed WordPress and WooCommerce on your host and need to lock down URL structure and plugin bloat before adding products.
steps: Go to Settings > Permalinks and select 'Post name' so product and page URLs read as /product-name/ rather than /?p=123. This matters for SEO and for customers sharing product links.

Go to the Plugins screen and use bulk actions to deactivate and delete default plugins that ship with the host's WordPress install and aren't needed (e.g., sample/hello-world plugins, bundled marketing or AI plugins you won't use).
After permalink changes, verify a product page and a category page load correctly, because some hosts need a .htaccess or server rewrite refresh.
Confirm your SSL is active before launching checkout, since permalink and rewrites interact with HTTPS redirects on most hosts.
caveats: The exact plugin names bundled by a host vary; verify which plugins are truly safe to delete before bulk-deleting.
Some managed hosts force a permalink structure or manage rewrites themselves.

cards.title: Set origin-based vs destination-based tax correctly per state
cards.summary: Cross-reference TaxJar to determine whether each state taxes by shop base address or customer shipping address, then enter rates with four decimal places in WooCommerce.
cards.use_when: You're configuring WooCommerce tax rates and need to decide which address WooCommerce should use as the tax basis for each state you sell into.
steps: Use TaxJar (or a similar reference) to look up each state's tax rule and confirm whether the state is origin-based or destination-based.

In WooCommerce, go to WooCommerce > Settings > Tax and choose the 'Calculate tax based on' option. For origin-based states, select 'Shop base address' so tax is computed from where your business is. For destination-based states, select 'Customer shipping address' so tax follows the buyer's location.
Add tax rates with four decimal places (e.g., 7.2500), matching how WooCommerce expects rate entry.
Test a cart with a shipping address in each type of state to confirm the tax line matches your expectation.
For multi-state selling, use tax tables/rates per state rather than a single blanket rate.
caveats: WooCommerce's setting is global; if you ship to both origin- and destination-based states, you need per-state rate tables plus rules, not just one setting.
TaxJar data and state rules change; re-verify rates periodically or use an automated tax service for accuracy.

cards.title: Charge flat-rate shipping per item instead of per order
cards.summary: Use the [qty] shortcode in WooCommerce's flat-rate cost field to multiply a dollar amount by the number of items in the cart.
cards.use_when: You want shipping priced per unit (e.g., heavy or bulky goods) rather than a flat charge for the whole order.
steps: In WooCommerce, go to Settings > Shipping, create or edit a shipping zone, and add a Flat Rate method.
In the Flat Rate cost field, enter a formula such as [qty] * 10 where 10 is your per-item dollar amount, so each item adds $10 to shipping.
Save and test with a two-item and three-item cart to confirm the shipping line scales as expected.
Combine with shipping classes if different product types need different per-item amounts.
caveats: [qty] counts total cart quantity; if you need per-weight or per-dimension pricing, use weight/dimension-based rules instead.
Free-shipping thresholds or coupons can interact with flat-rate formulas; test combinations.

cards.title: Install Stripe and PayPal via dedicated third-party plugins, not defaults
cards.summary: The source recommends skipping WooCommerce's bundled payment plugins and installing 'Payment Plugins for Stripe WooCommerce' and 'Payment Plugins for PayPal WooCommerce' for API-key setup.
cards.use_when: You're connecting card and PayPal payments and deciding which gateway plugin to install and how to enter API credentials.
steps: In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New and search for 'Payment Plugins for Stripe WooCommerce'; install and activate it. Repeat for 'Payment Plugins for PayPal WooCommerce'.

For Stripe: obtain your Publishable Key and Secret Key from your Stripe dashboard, then in the plugin go to Stripe API Settings, paste the Publishable Key, paste the Secret Key, and run the provided Connection Test.
Confirm the connection test passes before going live; a failed test usually means a wrong key or a test/live key mismatch.
Repeat the analogous API-key flow in the PayPal plugin, using your PayPal app credentials.
Place a live test transaction (small amount) and refund it to confirm the full capture and refund path works before launch.
caveats: This is the presenter's recommendation; default WooCommerce gateway plugins also exist and may suit simpler setups.
Plugin interfaces and menu names change — verify the current settings paths in your installed version.
Never paste live secret keys into a shared or test environment you don't control.

cards.title: Create global product attributes before building variable products
cards.summary: For variable products, define attributes globally first, then attach them to the product and generate variations with individual SKUs, images, prices and stock.
cards.use_when: You're creating a variable product (e.g., apparel with sizes and colors) and need a repeatable, correctly ordered workflow.
steps: Go to Products > Attributes and create global attributes (e.g., Weight, Toy Option, Size, Color) with their terms. Do this globally rather than only at the product level so attributes can be reused across the catalog.
Open the product and set Product data to 'Variable product'.
Add the existing global attributes on the Attributes tab and check 'Used for variations' for each one you want to generate combinations from.
Click 'Generate variations' to create the full combination set, then assign each variation its own SKU, image, price and stock.
Ensure every variation has a price, because a variation with no price is not purchasable.
Save and check the product page to confirm all desired variations appear and are selectable.
caveats: Generating all combinations can create many variations for multi-attribute products; prune unused combinations.
Global attributes are the recommended pattern, but product-level (custom) attributes still exist and may be fine for one-off products.

input.text:
05-SET / store and domain setup

Goes here. Going from nothing to a live store. Domain setup, WordPress configuration, WooCommerce initialization, tax and shipping profile logic, payment gateway API connections (Stripe/PayPal), and product creation (simple, variable, virtual, and affiliate).

Not here. • Elementor page builder design, CSS injection, and landing page layouts -> 07-LPG • Theme customization, header/footer configuration, color palettes, and global typography -> 04-BRD • Setting up blog post categories and content creation -> 13-ORG

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Provides the exact click paths for setting up WooCommerce on Hostinger, including manual origin/destination tax rules, quantity-based shipping rates, and third-party Stripe/PayPal API integrations. modules: [SET] topics: [domain and email, store configuration, payments and tax, shipping profiles] tier: 1 scope_hint: baseline

Topics. domain and email, store configuration, payments and tax, shipping profiles.

Look for.

WordPress Core Setup: The exact click path to optimize URLs (Settings > Permalinks > Post name) and disable default plugins via bulk actions.

WooCommerce Tax Configuration: The mechanics of setting up tax rates by cross-referencing TaxJar. Differentiating between origin-based states (calculating tax based on "Shop base address") and destination-based states (calculating tax based on "Customer shipping address"). The requirement to enter tax rates with four decimal places (e.g., 7.2500).

Quantity-Based Shipping: The exact formula to charge flat-rate shipping on a per-item basis instead of per-order within WooCommerce: enter [qty] * 10 (where 10 is the dollar amount) in the shipping cost field.

Payment Gateway Integration: The recommendation to skip default WooCommerce payment plugins and instead search for and install "Payment Plugins for Stripe WooCommerce" and "Payment Plugins for PayPal WooCommerce." The exact click path for Stripe: Stripe API Settings > paste Publishable Key > paste Secret Key > run Connection Test.

Variable Product Creation: The specific order of operations for variable products: First go to Products > Attributes to create global attributes (e.g., Weight, Toy Option) rather than doing it at the product level. Then inside the product, select "Variable product", add the existing global attributes, check "Used for variations", and finally click "Generate variations" to assign individual SKUs, images, and prices (noting that a variation must have a price to be purchasable).

Skip. Hostinger pricing breakdowns, discount codes (e.g., JFD10), and onboarding wizard surveys. Elementor Pro pricing tier comparisons. Step-by-step element styling (e.g., changing font sizes, border radiuses, adding SVG icons). All CSS copy-paste instructions. Pitches for third-party template marketplaces like KitNinja or KitPapa.

Scope mix. Nearly all baseline.

Volume. 10 to 15.
